previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with worsening back pain and fecal and urinary incontinence in the setting of known spinal compression fractures. MRI showed no new fractures or cord compression, but worsening of the T7 vertebral body fracture with retropulsion and spinal canal narrowing. Pain was poorly controlled on her home regimen of MS Contin and Dilaudid, and she experienced drowsiness and dizziness. The pain regimen was transitioned to a fentanyl patch with breakthrough Dilaudid, which improved control without sedation. She received IVIG for hypogammaglobulinemia and was found to have orthostatic hypotension, likely medication-related, which improved after discontinuing morphine. Transaminitis led to holding atorvastatin and fluconazole. Bowel and bladder incontinence resolved during admission. She was discharged home with a TLSO brace, rolling walker, and follow-up plans including a DXA scan and specialist visits.
